about: Single source for /dev-kit:help and the generated docs (docs/skills.md, docs/recipes.md, docs/glossary.md). English only; the help skill answers in the user's language. Edit here, then run: python3 -I skills/core/scripts/dev_docs.py build

categories.title: Bugs, changes and what is pending

skills.name: start
skills.one_line: Entry point: starts a new project, adopts an existing codebase (feature, maintenance or import mode) or resumes, and routes to the next skill.
skills.when: First command in any project, and whenever you come back and want to know where things stopped.

args.meaning: a project idea starts the interview; in an existing codebase it is the goal of the change, after the onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline)
resume: reconcile with git and route

examples.what: new project: git init if needed, then the interview

examples.command: /dev-kit:start add CSV export to the reports page
examples.what: existing codebase without .dev/: onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline, retroactive ADRs), then a short interview about the change

skills.produces: routing only; starts a session in the log

skills.name: help
skills.one_line: Help inside Claude Code: what to do next, how each skill works, recipes and concepts.
skills.when: Whenever you are unsure which skill to use or what something means.

args.meaning: next steps for this project and the skill map
the recipe or concept that answers it
the agents and who calls them
a term such as gate, buffer or baseline: its definition

examples.what: how to report bugs and improvements

examples.command: /dev-kit:help how do I run it overnight?

skills.name: interview
skills.one_line: Exhaustive requirements interview in 10 blocks; everything goes to .dev/brief.md with the autonomy policy.
skills.when: Beginning of a project (start calls it), or later to answer questions the kit parked.

args.meaning: one round with the 4 most important questions

examples.what: resolve what the kit parked or assumed

skills.name: status
skills.one_line: Read-only dashboard: lifecycle phase and step, next release, milestones, gates, scores, issues, preview, production drift, cost so far.
skills.when: Any time you want a quick picture of the project.

skills.name: board
skills.one_line: Live board in the browser, laid out like the flow diagram (docs/dev-kit-flow.svg): its tabs are the lanes - conception, planning, construction in two (milestones and releases) and stable - plus a Map with all five lanes at once, and it opens on the lane where the project is. Each screen fits the window without scrolling: on top the lane's steps as a flow, coloured by who does them (yours in yellow, agents in orange, delivery in green, gates in red), with where the project is, what runs and what waits on you; below, blocks of the same size, where what does not fit opens with "See all". Conception shows its documents, the PRD and design reviews, decisions and facts, and scope changes; planning the roadmap by release, the backlog and the plan review, with a screen of its own to replan by dragging tasks, issues and milestones; milestones the milestone picked (grouped by release) with its stages, the task board in columns of equal height or its QA rounds, and burndown, velocity and gates in a Metrics modal; releases the release picked with its stages (checks, audit, review, your approval, production, released) and its numbers, milestones, blockers and documents; stable the project totals, production, the health check, release flags, release checks and releases. "Needs you" is a button in the top bar that turns red (and rings once) when something waits, with a badge on the lane and on the step it belongs to; it opens a drawer with every item and its buttons (Approve and Reject for a release). Requests and activity are drawers too. Every link to a document of .dev/ opens it formatted in a side panel. Buttons ask Claude Code for work (run the next step, new issue, answer a question, a plan draft) and start it in the session that opened the board; the Autopilot switch in the top bar runs /dev-kit:autopilot from the board, one milestone per run, until a release waits for your approval, waiting on Needs you when only your decisions are left; hovering Live lists what is running; light or dark, English or Portuguese; local, shared on your network with an access link, or behind your reverse proxy.
skills.when: When you want to watch the project visually or drive it from the browser, e.g. away from the console; it updates by itself.

args.meaning: start the local server (or reuse the running one) and open the default browser
stop the server (the page also has a Stop server button)
whether it is running, its URL and PID
force a new tab, do not open a tab, preferred port (default 8765)
listen address (default 127.0.0.1); 0.0.0.0 shares the board on the network, opened only with the access link it prints
stop after N minutes with no open tab (default 120; 0 = never)
host name of your reverse proxy in front of the board (remembered for the project; none forgets it)
let the page queue requests to Claude Code (on by default; off makes the board show the project only)

examples.what: open the board; calling it again does not start a second server or a second tab
share it on your network (phone, another computer) with a private access link

skills.produces: nothing in the project by itself (requests are run by /dev-kit:worker: in the session that listens, or in a headless session the board starts itself when none does); its own files in .dev/run/

skills.name: worker
skills.one_line: Runs the requests you queued on the board (run a command, new issue, answer a question, plan draft, release approval or rejection) in this Claude Code session, one at a time; questions that would stop the run go to the board with answers to pick.
skills.when: It starts by itself, each time a request arrives: in the session that opened the board with /dev-kit:board, or, when no session listens, in a headless session the board starts (autonomy.board_executor). Run it by hand in another session only when the board says it cannot start Claude Code.

args.meaning: run every request waiting on the board, in order, until none is left or the queue is paused

examples.what: run what you asked for on the board

skills.produces: whatever each request does (commits, issues, plan changes); the request's result on the board

skills.name: prd
skills.one_line: Product requirements with user stories and numbered acceptance criteria (AC-n).
skills.when: After the interview, or to revise requirements when scope changes.

examples.what: write the PRD from the brief

skills.name: architecture
skills.one_line: Stack, repository layout, data model, contracts, environments, deploy commands and ADRs.
skills.when: After the PRD passes review, or when a structural decision must be revisited.

skills.name: ux
skills.one_line: Information architecture, journeys, every screen state, forms and microcopy guide.
skills.when: Products with a UI, after architecture, or to redesign a flow.

skills.name: ui
skills.one_line: Design tokens, components with states, and a spec for every screen (responsive, dark mode, accessibility).
skills.when: After ux, or to (re)specify a screen or component.

skills.name: plan
skills.one_line: Milestones M1..Mn and small vertical-slice tasks T-xxx with dependencies, ACs and files.
skills.when: After design (or architecture for UI-less products), and to replan remaining work.

args.meaning: rewrite only todo tasks of future milestones
add the risk fields to tasks already planned, without replanning
propose an exit_check for each open milestone of an older plan

examples.what: existing plan, before the next milestone

skills.name: review
skills.one_line: Scored independent review (0-100, with cut-off) of the PRD, design, plan or docs, looping until it passes.
skills.when: Before implementation (prd, design, plan) and before release (docs).

examples.what: score the PRD and revise until it passes

skills.name: autopilot
skills.one_line: Drives the build on its own: conception and planning, then milestone after milestone and the next release, until the project is stable; pauses follow your autonomy settings.
skills.when: After the interview, when you want the app built with minimal interaction (also overnight).

args.meaning: stop at a step: prd, architecture, design, plan, qa, usability, docs or release (e.g. plan, to review the documents first)
stop after N approved gates, to resume in a fresh session (cheaper long runs)
implementers at once for this run (1-6); without it, the number set on the board's Autopilot card (default 3). With the board's Autopilot running, it changes that run's number instead
how the board's Autopilot switch runs it: headless, questions go to Needs you, ends saying why (you do not type it)

examples.what: only the documents, so you can review them
one milestone, e.g. to gauge cost
two milestones, then resume in a new session

skills.produces: everything below, one commit per task

skills.name: implement
skills.one_line: Implements ready tasks test-first, full suite, one commit per task; hotfix lane first.
skills.when: To build tasks by hand instead of autopilot, or to run a specific task (e.g. a fix).

args.meaning: N isolated implementers in git worktrees; --parallel auto takes the number set on the board's Autopilot card (default 3)
work past a pending gate (records an ADR and sets the gate skipped)
internal: the milestone runs in a child session started by `dev_state.py round run`

skills.produces: code, tests, one commit per task

skills.name: test
skills.one_line: Test strategy and test writing: plan, missing tests for a task or path, flaky tests.
skills.when: Tests are missing, failing or flaky, or you want to define the testing approach.

args.meaning: cover a task or a folder

examples.what: add missing tests for a folder

skills.name: qa
skills.one_line: Milestone gate: auditors in parallel, 0-100 score per dimension, fix tasks until the cut-off is met.
skills.when: When a milestone's tasks are done, or to check one task (e.g. after a hotfix).

args.meaning: audit everything again, without reusing earlier clean reviews
internal: one round in a child session started by `dev_state.py round run`

skills.name: usability
skills.one_line: Whole-product audit of usability, accessibility, visuals and copy, with score and fix tasks.
skills.when: After the UI milestones are built, before release.

skills.name: issue
skills.one_line: Report a bug, improvement or scope change in plain words; the kit classifies and routes it without breaking the milestone cadence.
skills.when: You found a bug or want something to work differently, during or after the build.

examples.command: /dev-kit:issue "the Save button on the profile page does nothing"

examples.what: turn a deferred finding into an issue

skills.name: backlog
skills.one_line: Everything pending: hotfix, issue queue, next buffer, tasks, parked questions, deferred findings, deploys.
skills.when: You want to know what is left or what to do next.

examples.what: the full list and the recommended next step

skills.name: settings
skills.one_line: Shows and changes the project's settings in plain words: autonomy, quality bar, rounds, reuse, checks, deploys, tips, status line and notifications.
skills.when: You want the kit more or less autonomous or strict, to turn something on or off, or to see the configuration.

examples.what: see how the kit is configured
unattended level with the floors kept

skills.produces: the changed setting in .dev/state.json and an ADR for decisions

skills.name: deploy
skills.one_line: Production deploy of an approved milestone or release: preflight, backup, dry-run, install, migrations, smoke checks.
skills.when: After a gate when the project deploys per milestone, at release, or to check how far production is behind.

args.meaning: preflight and the method's own dry-run; nothing installed or recorded
run the production health check now, and offer to schedule it
turn the release flag of R2 off in production (release flags on)

skills.produces: deploy record shown by status; the health check result (.dev/run/prod-health.json) and, on failure, one expedite issue

skills.name: docs
skills.one_line: Project documentation from the artifacts and code: README, user guide, API reference, CHANGELOG.
skills.when: Before a release, or when you need docs for the project.

skills.name: release
skills.one_line: Ships the next release (the milestones closed since the last release, or the next planned release): audits, the release review and your approve/reject decision for a planned release, then version, CHANGELOG, tag, production deploy and the release record; patch releases for hotfixes.
skills.when: Between milestones, when closed milestones wait for the next release or a planned release has all its milestones closed (the board and status show it), to approve or reject a release waiting for you, or after a hotfix.

args.meaning: patch release for a closed hotfix
approve the planned release waiting for you
reject it; each line of feedback becomes a fix task

examples.what: check, audit and submit the next planned release for your approval (or decide on the one waiting)

examples.command: /dev-kit:release --reject "the error message on duplicate email is unclear"
examples.what: send the release back with what must change
ship a hotfix as a patch version

skills.produces: version bump, release notes, tag, release record (nothing waits any more; with nothing open the project is stable)

skills.name: costs
skills.one_line: Token usage and estimated US$ (API-equivalent) per stage, agent, model or session; CSV of tokens.
skills.when: You want to know how much was spent and where.

args.meaning: time per agent and skill, and what the work ledger reused

examples.what: cost of this session by stage
whole project by agent, with CSV
where the time went, and how much rework was avoided

skills.name: feedback
skills.one_line: Evaluation of the session: grade per stage with reasons, what worked and failed, suggestions for the kit.
skills.when: After a run, to review it or to send feedback to the dev-kit author.

recipes.title: Build a new app
steps: /dev-kit:start <your idea> and answer the interview
/dev-kit:autopilot --until plan, then read the PRD, design and plan
/dev-kit:autopilot to build the rest
/dev-kit:status at any time

recipes.title: Adopt dev-kit in an existing project
steps: Commit or stash pending work, then /dev-kit:start <the change you want> in the repository root
Onboarding: baseline tag dev-kit-baseline, .dev/discovery.md (stack, conventions, existing docs), test baseline, ADRs discovered/imported
Pick the entry mode: feature (new capability), maintenance (bugs only: straight to /dev-kit:issue) or import (use the project's PRD/specs/ADRs)
A stage was skipped? The lifecycle step is the first missing artifact and /dev-kit:start routes there; a stage that does not apply is recorded as review n/a
QA scores only what changed since the baseline; pre-existing problems become intangible issues

recipes.title: Let it run overnight
steps: Choose 'unattended with floors' in the interview, or later: /dev-kit:settings run overnight without asking
Cover permission prompts: /fewer-permission-prompts and --permission-mode acceptEdits
Run inside tmux: claude --permission-mode acceptEdits "/dev-kit:autopilot"
In the morning: /dev-kit:status, /dev-kit:backlog, /dev-kit:costs, /dev-kit:interview --gaps

recipes.title: I found a bug
steps: /dev-kit:issue "what happens and where"
Confirm the class the kit proposes (hotfix, current, standard, intangible)
Hotfix: /dev-kit:implement T-xxx → /dev-kit:qa --scope T-xxx → /dev-kit:deploy → /dev-kit:release --hotfix
Otherwise it waits in the queue for the next milestone's buffer or the cool-down

recipes.title: I want an improvement
steps: /dev-kit:issue "what should be better"
Standard improvements enter the next milestone's buffer; small ones the cool-down
See the queue with /dev-kit:backlog issues

recipes.title: Change the scope (new feature, different behaviour)
steps: /dev-kit:issue "the new behaviour" (class change)
Accept the chain prd → review prd → (ux/ui → review design) → plan replan: conception and planning are reopened, while the milestone in construction keeps going
The new tasks land in future milestones; the cadence does not change

recipes.title: What is left to do?
steps: /dev-kit:backlog for everything pending and the recommended next step
/dev-kit:status for the overall picture

recipes.title: How much did it cost?
steps: /dev-kit:costs for this session by stage
/dev-kit:costs --all --by agent for the whole project
/dev-kit:costs --csv to apply your own prices

recipes.title: Put it in production
steps: Answer the production questions in the interview (method, host, when, smoke checks, prerequisites)
/dev-kit:deploy --check to see the drift
/dev-kit:deploy M3 or let autopilot deploy per milestone
/dev-kit:deploy --health to check production now (the board checks it on schedule while it is open)

recipes.title: Deploy each milestone before its release (release flags)
steps: /dev-kit:settings: turn on release flags with your flag provider, and set production to per_milestone_flagged
/dev-kit:plan (or replan): every task of a release gets flag: release_R<n>, created off by sync-plan
each milestone goes to production when its gate passes, with the flag still off
approve the release: the flag is turned on, and a chore to remove it is planned in the next release; /dev-kit:deploy --rollback R2 turns it off again

recipes.title: Resume after a crash or a reboot
steps: /dev-kit:start to reconcile state with git
/dev-kit:autopilot continues from the current lifecycle step (status shows it)
/dev-kit:start also stops processes and frees locks left by the crash

recipes.title: Review the session or send feedback to the author
steps: /dev-kit:feedback writes a graded report and an export without project data
Review both files in .dev/feedback/ before sending them

recipes.title: Change autonomy, quality or other settings
steps: /dev-kit:settings <what you want, in words> (level, quality bar, rounds, reuse, task checks, buffer, deploys, tips)
/dev-kit:interview --gaps to revisit product decisions

recipes.title: See progress in Claude Code itself (tips, status line, notifications)
steps: /dev-kit:settings status line (or spinner tips, notifications, session title) turns each one on or off
Spinner tips and the status line go to .claude/settings.local.json, which stays out of git; tips show from the next session
After each skill, the greyed-out suggestion in the prompt is usually the next /dev-kit command: press Tab or Right arrow, then Enter

recipes.title: Watch the project on a board (or share it)
steps: /dev-kit:board opens the live board in the browser (one server per project)
/dev-kit:board --host 0.0.0.0 shares it on your network: open the access link it prints on the other device
/dev-kit:board stop (or the Stop server button) when done

recipes.title: Drive the work from the board
steps: /dev-kit:board in a Claude Code session opens the board and makes that session listen (keep it open, e.g. in tmux); away from the machine use an SSH tunnel, --host 0.0.0.0 with the access link, or --trusted-host behind your reverse proxy
on the board: Run next to a command, New issue, answer a question in Needs you, Plan to drag tasks and issues between milestones (or milestones between releases) and Send, or Go on by itself

each request starts in the listening session by itself; questions come back to the board with answers to pick. With no session listening, the board starts a headless Claude Code session for them by itself

recipes.title: Ship a release
steps: When every milestone of a planned release has passed its gate, /dev-kit:status (or the board) shows the release ready
/dev-kit:release --dry-run to see the checklist and the version it would use
/dev-kit:release runs usability (UI apps), docs and the release audit, writes releases/R<n>/review.md and waits for you
Approve on the board (Needs you) or with /dev-kit:release: production deploy, smoke, tag; or reject with what must change (a fixes milestone in the same release)

recipes.title: Check that the app is usable and accessible
steps: /dev-kit:usability (or --url http://localhost:3000 for an app already running)
/dev-kit:implement to run the fix tasks it created
/dev-kit:usability again until review ux passes

glossary.definition: Acceptance criterion, numbered AC-n in the PRD; every task and test points to the ACs it satisfies.
Architecture decision record in .dev/decisions.md; source auto, user, interview, policy, discovered or imported.

Where the project is: conception (interview, PRD, architecture, UX, UI) → planning (plan) → construction (milestones and the next release) → stable. A cycle, not a line: a scope change reopens conception and planning while construction goes on; a bug or improvement goes straight to construction. Derived from .dev/, never set by hand.

The first planned release not released yet; when all its milestones have passed their gates, release audits it and writes its release review for your approval. Releases cut before 3.0 are kept under R0.

A group of 2 to 5 milestones under a '## R<n>' heading of plan.md that delivers a complete value journey; a critical delivery (payments, auth, sensitive migration) ends one. Milestones of a later release start only after the earlier one is released.

The one human gate of construction: when every milestone of a planned release is closed, release writes its release review and waits; you approve (production deploy, smoke, record) or reject with what must change (a fixes milestone in the same release).

The document release writes for a release waiting for your approval (releases/R<n>/review.md): what it delivers against the PRD, milestones, confirmations, how to try it, quality and security, verified facts, risks, and your decision.

A flag named release_R<n> that keeps a release's code switched off in production until you approve the release (autonomy.release_flags, production.when per_milestone_flagged); removed by a chore in the next release.
production.health: a command or URL checked every interval_min by prod-check (on the board while it is open); a failure opens one expedite issue.
Lifecycle phase with nothing open: no milestone in progress, no queued issue, everything built is released. The next issue or change starts the cycle again.
Confirm PRD and Confirm plan: after a passed review, you confirm the document on the board or ask for changes; no milestone starts before the plan is confirmed.

A cadence step M1, M2… inside construction; the next one starts only after the previous gate passes. Building and QA belong to the milestone, not to the project phase. Issues never renumber milestones.
The quality check at the end of a milestone (qa): passes only with no critical/high findings and every score above its cut-off.
The exit_check of a milestone in plan.md: a test, a command or acceptance criteria that must pass at its gate (pass or fail, never a score).
What every milestone gate needs before any score counts: the build passes, the test suite passes and no secret is in the diff.
Minimum score for a gate or review, set in the interview (standard 85, premium 92, prototype 70).
From round 2, auditors verify whether previous findings were closed; new low findings are recorded but not scored.
Round 2+ of a review: blocking findings and the medium trend versus the previous round; a review converged twice can stop.
A PRD, architecture, design or plan whose sources changed after it was last updated; review brings it up to date before any reviewer runs.
Where an auditor writes its result (given in its prompt); the kit validates it, and the agent answers in a few lines.
Self-check plus cheap copy and static a11y agents at the end of each UI task (autonomy.task_checks), so the gate confirms instead of discovers.
A green suite stored per commit; the test auditor and the gate reuse it until the code it covers changes.
Record of verified work with the fingerprint of its inputs; only unchanged work that was clean is reused, with spot checks.
Suite, lint, type-check, data smoke and screenshots run once per QA round and read by every auditor.
An auditor not re-run in a later round (no open finding, nothing changed in its dimension); its result is kept.
What a task provides to others (table, route, fields), written in plan.md as contract: and given to the tasks that consume it.
A text an AC fixes, marked [locked] in the PRD; copy and visual reviews never reword it.
Something one agent may use at a time (remote session, shared DB, emulator), listed in the architecture and locked while in use.
A problem in shared code the milestone did not change; it becomes an issue and does not score in the gate.
changelog.d/T-xxx.md written by a task instead of CHANGELOG.md, merged by docs and release; no merge conflicts.
Playwright with mocks that captures every screen and state (qa:shots) and runs axe (qa:a11y); added by plan to the first UI milestone.
Low findings cost at most 10 points per dimension.
How an issue is scheduled: expedite (hotfix), current, standard (buffer), intangible (cool-down) or change (replan).
Share of each milestone (default 20%) reserved for queued issues.
Optional short slot after a gate where small issues are fixed before the next milestone.
Expedite lane for critical/high bugs in delivered work: one at a time, scoped QA, patch release.
Priority lane of a task: hotfix runs first, then cool-down, then the plan.
Per-agent isolation number that gives each agent its own port, database and scratch folder.

Pause-point action: never wait; record the question with the recommended answer, block only what depends on it and continue (the default of most points under the unattended level, available at any level).
What the kit does at each pause point: ask, preauthorize within a limit, apply the recommendation, or park.
Agents start on their base model and effort; failed dimensions are re-run one step higher, with consent.
Estimated US$ of the tokens at API prices; on subscription plans nothing is billed per token.
.dev/telemetry.jsonl: structured, high-level events of the run, without project data.
The git tag dev-kit-baseline set by the onboarding: everything before it is legacy, everything after it is new work that QA scores.

An existing project not built with dev-kit. start runs the onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline, entry mode); audits score only the changes since the baseline and legacy problems become issues (conventions §16).
A finding in code that existed before dev-kit (existing projects): reported with "legacy": true, never scored, turned into an issue.
How an existing project is adopted: feature (new capability), maintenance (bugs and small improvements through issues) or import (existing PRD/specs are the source).
In maintenance mode, the milestone M<n> — Maintenance that issues fill; its gate runs like any other, then the next issue opens M<n+1>.
Tags of ACs and screens in existing projects: existing works already (no task), changed gets a task, new is built from scratch.
A review that does not apply (e.g. design with no new UI); recorded with a note, it satisfies prerequisites and is not graded.
The onboarding report of an existing project (.dev/discovery.md): stack, layout, commands, conventions, existing docs and ADRs.
production.method external: the project's own CI/CD deploys; the kit only confirms and records the commit.
The approved milestone built and run on 127.0.0.1 (keep_running or smoke), per autonomy.local_deploy.
A task removed by a replan: kept for history, never counted by milestones, next or release.
The private URL printed by /dev-kit:board --host 0.0.0.0; other devices open the shared board only through it.
The board's estimate of when the open work finishes (probable and late dates) and what it costs, from the pace and cost of the milestones done.
The class of service for a critical/high bug in delivered work: a hotfix task that runs before everything (WIP 1).
Claude Code's greyed-out guess of your next prompt; every dev-kit report ends with the next command so it is offered. Tab or Right arrow takes it.
Line under the Claude Code prompt; the dev-kit one shows the lifecycle phase (with the step in conception and planning), milestone progress, the running task and the next command.
